The most likely corrupted element is **M1**, the fb-side input device of the error-amp differential pair. Its length is 0.15 µm, while its partner M2 (same W, vref side) is 1.914 µm. That mismatch gives the pair a systematic threshold offset of roughly 27 mV, which at the divider (gain of 2) produces the observed 1.145 V output, a 4.6% error. The short L on M1 also lowers its output resistance and the error-amp gain, which is consistent with the weak 1 kHz PSRR. The first-order check is that the feedback divider (R1 = R2) and the mirror (M3/M4) are consistent with the target, so the error is in the amplifier input pair.
